note: One route, two widths, and a fixture it cannot photograph without. `/collection/replace/summary/[uploadId]` needs a CONFIRMED upload carrying a summary_payload, and the contested section only draws where committed demand exceeds supply — the headless probe account has no committed deck at all, so a run with no fixture photographs a working feature as an empty one. `pnpm seed:summary <userId>` writes that fixture (two committed decks a month apart, and a receipt with all three sections populated) and prints the URL; it takes --clean. SUMMARY_UPLOAD comes from the environment for the same reason the other inventories take their deck id that way: no account's row id belongs in a checked-in file. The second row is the same route with its issues line opened, because IssueInspector reachable after the confirm is the one thing ruled IN scope for this PR that a still photograph of the page would otherwise miss. The third row exists because the phone's first screenful ends inside `Still to buy`: the contested section is the one thing this PR adds that a phone shot of the fold cannot show, and a row that photographs the top of the page reads as coverage while proving nothing about it. The fourth row presses an option, because the whole point of the chooser is what happens on the tap: the picked mark takes accent and the outcomes swap — neither of which a photograph of the default state can show. (The undo footer that used to appear here was retired on 2026-09-16: it offered to undo a pick of the deck that already held the card, where there is nothing to undo.) It leaves a reservation behind in the fixture account, which `pnpm seed:summary <userId> --clean` removes along with the rest. The two picked rows are ONE PER WIDTH, and each presses a DIFFERENT deck, which is not a stylistic choice: a row that writes cannot be run twice against the same state. The first version pressed the same deck at both widths, the second press toggled the first one off, and the desktop photograph showed the default allocation while reporting a pass. Pressing different decks leaves each width with a pick of its own — the second press moves the reservation rather than clearing it. `pnpm seed:summary <userId> --clean` clears what they leave behind. Their ids carry no width: the harness appends one, so a row called `…-phone` writes `…-phone-phone.png` and leaves the file a reader expects sitting there from the previous run — which is exactly how a stale photograph got read as a finding once. `CONTESTED_DECK` is no longer read here: it named the deck for a second door, on `/decks/[id]/changes`, that this inventory used to also photograph. That row and the `shares` block checking both doors rendered the same `ContestedCardRow` were both removed 2026-10-04 (Hugh, no Design round — a removal): that door's per-row panel is gone, and a replacement is going to Design separately. The import summary is this feature's only surface now, so there is nothing left to compare it against for drift.
